notes: Page budget (9) spent on the Republic page, Beiyang government, Northern Expedition, Nanjing decade, Second Sino-Japanese War, Chinese Civil War, Taiwan Retrocession Day, Manchukuo and Sheng Shicai. The Empire of China pages are cited in the empire-of-china dossier. ONE STATE OR TWO (Q148): the brief asks whether the Republic and the People's Republic (Cliopatria rows sharing Wikidata Q148) are one state. They are two: the Republic of China (1912-) continues on Taiwan to 2024 under its own government, the People's Republic was proclaimed on 1 October 1949 and took the mainland by May 1950. The ROC row and the PRC row stay apart; the Q148 on the ROC row is Cliopatria's mistake. THE KUOMINTANG ROW: Cliopatria's 'Kuomintang' (1917-1929) is a country-wide outline, not the KMT's land (see the kuomintang dossier, which cuts it to Guangdong and the expedition's gains). The Republic of China therefore gets new keyframes for 1916-1927 (the 1914 outline less the KMT's land) and has no keyframe for 1928-1929, which the kuomintang dossier carries (the Nationalist government is the Republic from 29 December 1928: merge event 1928, gain event 1930). THE EMPIRE: 1916 January to March is the empire-of-china dossier; the Republic is restored in March. OCCUPATION AND PUPPETS: the empire-of-japan dossier (jk-01) already carries Japan's occupation of the Republic's land and the vassals Manchukuo, Mengjiang and the East Hebei council; the Republic's occupation events mirror it with the same region specs (Cliopatria's Japanese shapes of 1938, 1939 and 1944). Not on the pages: Shandong and Shanxi (March 1938), Kaifeng (June 1938), Guangzhou (October 1938), Hainan (1939), Guangxi (1944), East Hebei (1935): see empire-of-japan. NOT ON THE PAGES: Tibet (1911-1913 independence; the 1912 shape holds 23% of Xizang), Outer Mongolia 1911-1919 and the Kyakhta Treaty, the Xinjiang Ili rising (events 1919-1921 and 1944 are conf 1 from the other dossiers), the dates of the Qing-to-Republic provinces, Yan'an's loss in 1948, Shandong in 1948, the Dachen Islands (1955) and Yijiangshan, Kinmen's 1949 battle date, the First and Second Taiwan Strait crises.
